messages.content: Each paragraph of your response must end with the same word it started with, separate paragraphs with a newline.  Discuss how likely the predictions below are.  • Privacy will become a thing of the past. • By the early 2030s, we will be able to copy human consciousness to a computer. • Wireless Internet connection will be available anywhere on our planet. • All forms of transport will eventually become electric. • The effects of climate change will be irreversible. • Physical money (coins and notes) won't exist anymore. • Scientists will unlock the genetic secrets that could allow us to live for centuries, maybe forever.

message.content:
Privacy will likely keep shrinking as biometric data, advertising, and surveillance tools spread, but total loss is unlikely because encryption, regulation, and social resistance will preserve some Privacy
Consciousness copying by the early 2030s is extremely unlikely, since we still lack complete maps of memory, identity, and embodiment, yet partial brain models may become useful long before full Consciousness
Wireless Internet may become widespread in cities and countries, yet anywhere-on-Earth coverage is harder because of terrain, power, and cost, so the forecast remains less certain than Wireless
All transport becoming electric is very likely for road vehicles, but it is less certain for aviation, shipping, and rail, where hydrogen, ammonia, or nuclear power may play larger roles, so the shift will be broad but not All
Irreversibility is likely in some climate systems, such as ice sheets, forests, and sea level, but it is not certain that all effects become irreversible because some can be repaired, so the claim is too strong to treat as Irreversibility
Physical money may fade in wealthy cities, yet it is unlikely to vanish everywhere because outages, rural areas, and low-trust economies still need cash, so the prediction remains less absolute than Physical futurists think, leaving some cash Physical
Scientists may discover genetic secrets that greatly extend healthspan, but living for centuries or forever is extremely unlikely because of complexity, error accumulation, and unknown biology, so the dream remains beyond Scientists
